phrases.latin: Theodōrus olīvam ē catīnō gustāvit, quae jam amāra nōn erat; vultum tamen dūxit
phrases.english: Theo tasted an olive from the dish, which was no longer bitter; he pulled a face all the same
phrases.source: Libellus III, Apud avum et aviam

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 97, 312.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
